name: Algeria
headline: Algeria: +3.9% growth in 2025, 1.4% inflation, debt 52% of GDP
sections: Algeria is a $284 billion economy (2025), the world's 52nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.9% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $19K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.5% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 1.4% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 9.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 11.6% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 29.4% (2025).
Gross government debt is 52% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has risen from 46% in 2020. The general government balance is −10.5% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −8.9% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 39% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 79% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.5 years (2024). Population: 47.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
